help.tagline: machine-wide locks for files, folders and names
help.intro: jlock lets programs, scripts, people and AI agents on one machine take turns. Before touching a file, a folder or any named resource (a port, a deploy), they ask jlock for its lock: one owner at a time, the others wait in line in order of arrival. A lock left by a process that died is recovered by itself, a request that would deadlock is refused, and jlock list shows who holds what. There is no server: the state is a folder on disk.
help.version: Print the version on one line (jlock 0.2.0).
help.global.json: Print one JSON object instead of text. It is the same in every language: scripts should read it.
help.global.lang: Language of the text output, for this run. Default: JLOCK_LANG, else the system's language, else English.
help.global.help: Help for the command it goes with (same as jlock help <command>).
help.keys: Keys: a path (a file or a folder, absolute or relative; a folder also covers everything inside it), name:<text> for anything that is not a path (name:port-3000), or * for everything.
help.more: jlock help <command> explains one command: every option with its default and an example, complete examples, and its exit codes.
help.also_global: Also: --lang <{tag}> for the language of the text, --help for this page.
help.opt.json: Print one JSON object with a result field instead of text lines.
help.exit.2: wrong usage: a bad option or value (the message says which)
help.exit.12: deadlock: waiting would close a cycle (the chain is printed)
help.exit.13: not the owner: the lock belongs to someone else, or to nobody
help.exit.14: lock lost: broken with unlock --force, or expired
help.exit.20: file system error (permission, disk full, a file held by another program); the OS message says which
help.exit.130: interrupted (CTRL+C) while waiting; the place in the queue was given up
help.cmd.acquire.summary: Take keys and keep them after the command ends.
help.cmd.acquire.desc: Takes every key given, all or none, in a fixed order, so two callers asking for the same keys in different orders never block each other. A free key is granted at once; a taken one is waited for in a fair queue, in order of arrival, without limit unless --timeout or --no-wait says otherwise. The lock stays after jlock exits: renew it with jlock heartbeat, or use hold or run, which renew it for you. Asking again for a key you already hold is granted at once.
help.cmd.acquire.examples:
# An agent takes two files before editing them
jlock acquire src/a.ts src/b.ts --owner agent-7 --group task-42 --intent "refactor"
# Try once; exit 10 if someone else has it
jlock acquire name:port-3000 --no-wait
# Wait at most 30 seconds
jlock acquire D:\proj\dist --timeout 30s
help.opt.acquire.owner: Who takes the lock. Whoever shows the same owner, from any process, can release or renew it. Default: pid:<pid of this jlock>.
help.opt.acquire.group: A label shared by related locks, to release or break them together (release --group). Default: none.
help.opt.acquire.intent: What the lock is for, in a sentence; status and list show it. Default: none.
help.opt.acquire.meta: Extra key=value data stored with the lock (repeat it for more); jlock does not read it. Default: none.
help.opt.acquire.ttl: Hard limit: the lock expires this long after it was granted, even if its owner is alive. Units: ms, s, m, h, d. Default: no limit. jlock renew pushes it back.
help.opt.acquire.wait: Wait in the queue until the keys are free. This is the default.
help.opt.acquire.no_wait: Do not wait: if a key is taken, answer busy (exit 10) with its holder and the place you would have had.
help.opt.acquire.timeout: Wait at most this long, then leave the queue and give up (exit 11). Units: ms, s, m, h, d. Default: no limit.
help.cmd.run.summary: Hold keys while a command runs, like flock(1).
help.cmd.run.desc: Takes the keys (with the same options as acquire), runs the command written after --, renews the lock while it runs and releases it when it ends. Everything after -- belongs to the command, even words that look like jlock options. jlock exits with the command's own exit code. If the lock is lost the command is stopped and run exits 14; if run itself is killed, the lock expires.
help.cmd.run.examples:
# One build at a time on this machine
jlock run D:\proj\dist -- cargo build --release
# Give up after waiting 2 minutes
jlock run name:deploy-prod --timeout 2m -- ./deploy.sh
help.exit.run.0: the command's own exit code, once the keys were granted (0 when it succeeds)
help.exit.run.14: lock lost while the command ran; the command was stopped
help.cmd.hold.summary: Hold keys until told to stop.
help.cmd.hold.desc: Takes the keys (with the same options as acquire), prints granted, then keeps running and renewing the lock. It releases and exits 0 when it reads the line release on its standard input, on CTRL+C, or when it is terminated; it also ends with 0 when its owner gives the keys back with jlock release. While it runs, the operating system also locks holder.json, so the lock is freed the moment the process dies. If the lock is taken away it prints lost and exits 14. With --detach it answers and returns at once, and a second process keeps the lock in the background: the simplest way for an agent to hold the files of a whole task.
help.cmd.hold.examples:
# An agent takes the files of its task: one call, the answer in hand
jlock hold src/a.ts src/b.ts --owner agent-7 --group task-42 --detach
# ... and gives them back at the end
jlock release --group task-42 --owner agent-7
# In the foreground, writing release to its standard input lets go
jlock hold name:deploy --owner ci
help.opt.hold.detach: Answer and return like acquire (granted, busy, timeout, with the same exit codes), while a second jlock hold keeps the lock alive in the background until jlock release, the --ttl, or unlock --force. One call for an agent, with the answer in hand.
help.opt.hold.release_on_eof: End when standard input closes: the end of the input counts as the line release, so a program that stays open and runs hold in the foreground, holding its standard input, lets go of the lock the moment it dies (even on Windows, where a dead parent does not end its children). Not with --detach: the background process has no standard input.
help.exit.hold.0: released, after release, CTRL+C or termination
help.cmd.release.desc: Gives back the keys named, if you are their owner (exit 13 otherwise). Without keys it releases everything the owner holds; with --group, everything the owner holds in that group. The next one in the queue gets each key, and a key's folder disappears once nobody holds or waits for it.
help.opt.release.owner: Whose locks to release. Default: pid:<pid of this jlock>, which only matches locks taken by this same process; pass the owner you acquired with.
help.opt.release.group: Release the owner's locks in this group (everybody's, with --any-owner).
help.opt.release.any_owner: With --group: release the group's locks, whoever owns them.
help.cmd.release.examples:
jlock release src/a.ts --owner agent-7
# Everything agent-7 holds
jlock release --owner agent-7
# The whole group, whoever owns each lock
jlock release --group task-42 --any-owner
help.exit.release.0: released (or there was nothing to release)
help.exit.release.13: a key named is not yours; the others were released
help.cmd.renew.summary: Push back the deadline of locks you hold.
help.cmd.renew.desc: Moves the deadline (--ttl) of locks you hold to now plus the ttl, and renews their heartbeat: for work that may outlast the ttl it asked for. Without --ttl it uses the ttl the lock was taken with. Without keys it renews everything the owner holds; with --group, everything the owner holds in that group. The lock is never let go while it is renewed, and a hold or run keeping it goes on as before. A lock already past its deadline cannot be renewed: it expires (exit 14) and has to be taken again.
help.opt.renew.owner: Whose locks to renew. Default: pid:<pid of this jlock>, which is rarely right: pass the owner.
help.opt.renew.group: Renew only the owner's locks in this group.
help.opt.renew.ttl: The new deadline, counted from now. Units: ms, s, m, h, d. Default: the ttl the lock was taken with.
help.cmd.renew.examples:
jlock renew src/a.ts --owner agent-7
# Everything agent-7 holds, for two more hours
jlock renew --owner agent-7 --ttl 2h
help.exit.renew.0: renewed (or there was nothing to renew)
help.exit.renew.13: a key named is not yours; the others were renewed
help.exit.renew.14: a lock was already past its deadline and expired; take it again
help.cmd.heartbeat.summary: Renew a lock taken with acquire.
help.cmd.heartbeat.desc: Tells jlock that the owner of a lock taken with acquire is still alive. A lock not renewed for JLOCK_STALE_MS (30 s by default) is taken for dead and expires. Call it more often than that, or use hold or run, which renew by themselves.
help.opt.heartbeat.owner: The owner the lock was taken with. Default: pid:<pid of this jlock>, which is rarely right: pass the owner.
help.exit.heartbeat.13: lost: the lock is not yours any more (broken or expired)
help.cmd.status.summary: Show who holds one key and who waits for it.
help.cmd.status.desc: Shows whether the key is free or held, and by whom: since when, the last heartbeat, the group and the intent. Then the queue, in order, and the other keys that block it: a folder above it, files inside it, or *. A dead lock found on the way is expired.
help.cmd.status.examples:
jlock status src/a.ts
jlock status name:port-3000 --json
help.cmd.list.summary: Show everything locked on this machine.
help.cmd.list.desc: Lists every key that is held or has a queue. It reads the registry folder itself, never a summary, so it is always the truth.
help.cmd.list.more: Columns: KEY the key. OWNER who holds it. GROUP and INTENT as given to acquire. HELD for how long. HEARTBEAT how long since the last renewal, marked (dead) when it stopped and nobody holds the OS lock (it will be expired), or (late) when it is late but the process is alive. QUEUE how many wait.
help.opt.list.owner: Only keys held or waited for by this owner.
help.opt.list.under: Only paths at or inside this folder.
help.opt.list.stale: Only dead locks and tickets (heartbeat older than JLOCK_STALE_MS, or past the ttl).
help.cmd.list.examples:
jlock list
jlock list --under D:\proj --watch
jlock list --owner agent-7 --json
help.cmd.graph.summary: Show who waits for whom, and any cycle.
help.cmd.graph.desc: Each line is one waiter, whom it waits for, and through which key. A cycle (A waits for B while B waits for A) is a deadlock; jlock refuses the request that would close one, so a cycle only shows for an instant.
help.cmd.unlock.desc: For emergencies: breaks the locks named, whoever owns them, and writes to the log who forced and why. The owner's hold or run notices at its next heartbeat and stops with 14, and the next one in the queue gets the key. To give back your own lock, use release.
help.opt.unlock.force: Required: confirms that you mean to break other people's locks.
help.opt.unlock.owner: Break every lock of this owner.
help.opt.unlock.group: Break every lock of this group.
help.opt.unlock.reason: Why, written to the log. Default: none.
help.opt.unlock.by: Who is forcing, written to the log. Default: user:<your login>.
help.cmd.unlock.examples:
jlock unlock D:\proj\src --force --reason "agent hung"
jlock unlock --owner agent-3 --force
help.exit.unlock.0: done (also when there was nothing to break)
help.cmd.gc.summary: Clean up now: expire dead locks, remove empty folders.
help.cmd.gc.desc: Runs the global sweep at once: expires locks and tickets whose owners died, deletes leftovers, removes empty key folders, rotates the log, rewrites index.json, and prints what it removed. Every command already does this, at most once every JLOCK_SWEEP_MS.
help.cmd.help.desc: Without a command: what jlock is and the list of commands. With a command: its options with defaults and examples, and its exit codes. jlock <command> --help shows the same page.
help.cmd.help.examples:
jlock help
jlock help acquire
jlock --lang pt-BR help run
help.exit.help.2: no such command (the closest name is suggested)
help.cmd.about.summary: Who made jlock, and where to find it.
help.cmd.about.desc: Prints the version, the author with GitHub and LinkedIn, the repository, the license and the links to the documentation. It does not use the network.
about.what: Machine-wide locks for files, folders and names: a fair queue, recovery of locks left by dead processes, deadlock detection, no server.
about.author: author
tip.busy: tip: jlock status {key} shows who holds it and the queue; drop --no-wait to wait your turn
tip.timeout: tip: wait longer with a bigger --timeout, or see who holds it with jlock status {key}
tip.deadlock: tip: release what you hold and ask again, or take all the keys in one acquire
tip.not_owner: tip: the lock belongs to {owner}; use --owner {owner}, or jlock unlock --force to break it
tip.lost: tip: someone broke or expired your lock on {key}; stop changing it, check jlock status {key}, and take it again with jlock acquire
help.cmd.update.summary: Install the latest release of jlock over this one.
help.cmd.update.desc: Asks GitHub for the latest release (or takes the version given), downloads the archive for this system, checks it against the SHA256SUMS of the release, puts the new jlock in place of the one running, and runs it once to confirm its version; if that fails, the old one is put back. It uses the system's curl (PowerShell on Windows when there is no curl). This is the only command that uses the network, and only when you run it.
help.cmd.update.examples:
# Is there a newer version?
jlock update --check
# Install it
jlock update
# Install one exact version (also an older one)
jlock update --version v0.1.0
help.opt.update.check: Only compare this version with the latest one; change nothing.
help.opt.update.version: Install this version instead of the latest one. Default: the latest release.
help.exit.update.0: updated, already up to date, or (with --check) compared
help.exit.update.20: no release found, download or checksum failed, or the folder cannot be written; the message says which
update.available: an update is available: jlock update installs it
update.no_tool: update needs curl (or PowerShell on Windows) in PATH
update.no_release: no release found at {url} (none published yet?)
update.cannot_write: cannot write in {dir}, where this jlock lives; run the update as an administrator (or with sudo), or install jlock in a folder of yours (install.ps1 -InstallDir, JLOCK_INSTALL_DIR)
update.not_in_sums: {asset} is not listed in the release's SHA256SUMS; nothing was changed
update.bad_sum: checksum mismatch for {asset} (expected {want}, got {got}); nothing was changed
update.check_failed: the new jlock answered '{answer}' to --version; the old one was put back
update.restore_failed: the new jlock did not work and the old one could not be put back at {path}; reinstall with install.sh or install.ps1
update.no_exe: cannot tell where this jlock is
help.cmd.doctor.summary: Check that this machine is ready for locks.
help.cmd.doctor.desc: Checks, in order: the version and the executable running; the registry folder (JLOCK_HOME), where it comes from, and whether it is a writable folder; the three file operations the protocol stands on (create_new, rename, remove) in that folder; the OS lock that hold and run use; the file system; the JLOCK_* variables; whether this jlock is the first one in PATH; what the registry holds now; and curl, for update. Each line says ok, warn or fail, and how to fix it. It only suggests: it never changes anything, and the only files it writes are its own temporary ones, removed before it ends.
help.exit.doctor.0: no check failed (warnings do not change the code)
doctor.home_set_fix: set JLOCK_HOME to the folder where the locks should live
doctor.home_missing_fix: create it with mkdir "{path}" (jlock gc, or any command that takes a lock, creates it too)
doctor.home_not_dir_fix: point JLOCK_HOME at a folder, or move the file {path} out of the way
doctor.home_readonly_fix: give your user permission to create and delete files in {path}, or set JLOCK_HOME to a folder you can write
doctor.primitives_fix: put JLOCK_HOME on a local disk (NTFS, ext4, APFS); network and FUSE file systems may not give these guarantees
doctor.primitives_ok: create_new refuses an existing file, rename replaces one, remove deletes
doctor.oslock_unsupported: this file system has no OS lock: hold and run fall back to the heartbeat alone
doctor.oslock_unsupported_fix: usually a network or FUSE file system; on a local disk the OS lock tells a frozen owner from a dead one
doctor.oslock_wrong: the OS lock does not keep out a second holder
doctor.oslock_ok: taken, refused to a second handle, then released
doctor.var_invalid: {name}={value} is not a positive number, so {default} is used
doctor.var_stale_heartbeat: JLOCK_STALE_MS ({stale}) is not above JLOCK_HEARTBEAT_MS ({heartbeat}): live locks would be taken for dead
doctor.var_poll_stale: JLOCK_POLL_MS ({poll}) is above JLOCK_STALE_MS ({stale}): waiters would be taken for dead
doctor.var_lang: JLOCK_LANG={value} is not a known language
doctor.var_unknown: {name} is not a jlock variable (a typo?)
doctor.vars: heartbeat {heartbeat} ms, stale after {stale} ms, poll {poll} ms, sweep every {sweep} ms, log up to {log} bytes, language {lang}
doctor.vars_fix: correct or unset the variables named; docs/USAGE.md lists them with their defaults
doctor.path_missing_fix: add {dir} to PATH, or install with install.sh / install.ps1
doctor.path_ok: this jlock is the first one in PATH
doctor.path_other: PATH finds {other} first; this one is {me}
doctor.path_other_fix: remove the other copy, or put this one's folder earlier in PATH
doctor.registry: {held} held, {queued} with a queue, {dead} dead; last sweep: {sweep}; log: {log} bytes
doctor.registry_debris: {unknown} folders without a readable key, {broken} with leftovers in broken/
doctor.registry_fix: run jlock gc to clean them up
doctor.curl_powershell: not found; jlock update will use PowerShell instead
doctor.curl_missing: not found: jlock update needs it
doctor.curl_missing_fix: install curl with your package manager; nothing else in jlock needs it
doctor.skipped: not checked: the registry folder is not usable
doctor.skipped_fix: fix the registry folder first (see above)
status.why_above: why: a lock on a folder covers everything inside it, so a held folder above this key blocks it
status.why_inside: why: a folder can only be taken when nothing inside it is, so these keys inside it block it
list.legend_dead: (dead) the heartbeat stopped and nobody holds the OS lock: it will be expired
list.legend_late: (late) the heartbeat is late, but the process holding the lock is alive (OS lock held)
warn.bad_ms: ignoring {name}={value} (want a positive number of ms)
warn.stale_vs_heartbeat: JLOCK_STALE_MS ({stale}) should be well above JLOCK_HEARTBEAT_MS ({heartbeat})
error.unknown_command_near: unknown command '{cmd}'; did you mean '{near}'? Commands: {list}
error.unknown_option_near: {cmd}: unknown option --{flag}; did you mean --{near}? (see jlock help {cmd})
error.eof_with_detach: hold: --release-on-eof does not go with --detach (the background process has no standard input)
error.cannot_detach: cannot start the background jlock hold
error.unlock_needs_force: unlock breaks other people's locks: add --force if that is what you mean (to give back your own lock, use jlock release)
error.no_localappdata: LOCALAPPDATA is not set; set JLOCK_HOME
error.no_home: HOME is not set; set JLOCK_HOME
